claims.text: Small adjustments in elemental composition can tune magnetic exchange interactions in non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Changing the relative amounts of magnetic and non-magnetic atoms can modify the magnetocaloric response.
The baseline non-equiatomic HEA exhibits a moderate magnetic transition.
The baseline non-equiatomic HEA exhibits a moderate magnetocaloric effect.
Minor compositional doping through increasing or decreasing Co or Fe content is a method for tuning the alloy.
Changing elemental concentrations alters the local chemical environment.
Changing elemental concentrations alters the distribution of magnetic clusters.
Changes in the local chemical environment and magnetic-cluster distribution alter interatomic exchange interactions.
Composition adjustment modifies the density and distribution of magnetic moments.
Composition adjustment influences magnetic anisotropy and exchange coupling.
Changes in magnetic moments, anisotropy, and exchange coupling shift the magnetic transition temperature, such as the Curie temperature.
Composition-induced magnetic changes affect the isothermal entropy change associated with the magnetocaloric effect.
Optimized compositions will exhibit enhanced magnetization changes near the modified transition temperature.
Optimized compositions will exhibit larger isothermal entropy changes and improved magnetocaloric performance relative to the baseline.
Excessive compositional deviation may induce phase instability or unwanted secondary phases.
Phase instability or unwanted secondary phases can limit magnetocaloric improvement.
